USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

A pediatric prescribing restriction

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

An 11-year-old child has pain after a fracture. During medication reconciliation, the pharmacist sees a proposed tramadol prescription. The child has normal renal function and no medication allergies. Which feature independently makes tramadol contraindicated under US labeling?

  1. No previous opioid exposure
  2. Age younger than 12 years
  3. Normal renal function
  4. Absence of drug allergies
  5. A fracture as the source of pain
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Age younger than 12 years

US tramadol labeling contraindicates use below age 12.

Understanding the options

Age younger than 12 years
US tramadol labeling contraindicates use below age 12.
Normal renal function
Normal renal function is not a contraindication.
Absence of drug allergies
A negative allergy history is not a contraindication.
A fracture as the source of pain
The injury itself is not the age-based contraindication being tested.
No previous opioid exposure
The specific absolute restriction here is age; opioid-naive adults are not universally excluded.
